title: Raise the resistance
hook: Change resistance and predict current magnitude.
misconception: current magnitude doubles when resistance doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply I = abs(V)/R to compare current magnitude when resistance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ohmic resistor at fixed voltage magnitude, I = abs(V)/R. When resistance doubles, current magnitude becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model I = abs(V)/R; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ohmic resistor at fixed voltage magnitude, with a nonzero initial result. If resistance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on current magnitude?
recall.why: Apply I = abs(V)/R under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
